1: //! # Incomplete Analysis: Linter-Internal Limit Checks
2: //!
3: //! This module implements the 17 "Incomplete Analysis" checks from MATLAB's Code
4: //! Analyzer. These are special internal-limit diagnostics that **cannot be disabled**
5: //! by the user. They all have default severity `Error`.
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                  | Detection                                  |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
11: //! | TMMSG    | More than 10,000 diagnostics generated       | Post-lint (diagnostic count > threshold)   |
12: //! | TMSMS    | More than 1,000 parse errors generated       | Count ERROR nodes in tree                  |
13: //! | MXASET   | File too complex to analyze                  | Node count > threshold                     |
14: //! | QUIT     | Analysis did not complete                    | No-op (linter panic guard)                 |
15: //! | NOSPC    | File too complex (nesting)                   | Max nesting depth > threshold              |
16: //! | MBIG     | File too large                               | Source length > threshold                  |
17: //! | NOFIL    | File not found                               | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
18: //! | MDOTM    | Invalid file extension                       | File extension != `.m`                     |
19: //! | MDMCR    | Deployed MATLAB file                         | File extension == `.ctf` or `.p`           |
20: //! | RDERR    | Unable to read file                          | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
21: //! | EOFER    | Too many syntax errors                       | ERROR node count > threshold               |
22: //! | EOFMI    | Incomplete file                              | Last node is ERROR or MISSING              |
23: //! | MDEEP    | Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply       | Max `()`, `[]`, `{}` nesting depth         |
24: //! | DEEPC    | Block comments nested too deeply             | Nested `%{ %}` detection                   |
25: //! | DEEPN    | Functions nested too deeply                  | Nested `function_definition` depth         |
26: //! | DEEPS    | Statements nested too deeply                 | Nested if/for/while/switch/try depth       |
27: //! | TEXTL    | Text too long                                | Max line length > threshold                |
28: //!
29: //! ## Configuration
30: //!
31: //! ```toml
32: //! [lint.rules.INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS]
33: //! max_diagnostics = 10000
34: //! max_parse_errors = 1000
35: //! max_node_count = 100000
36: //! max_file_size = 1048576
37: //! max_paren_depth = 32
38: //! max_function_depth = 20
39: //! max_statement_depth = 15
40: //! max_line_length = 4096
41: //! ```

137: /// Metrics gathered in a single traversal of the parse tree.
138: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
139: struct TreeMetrics {
140:     /// Total number of nodes in the tree.
141:     node_count: usize,
142:     /// Number of ERROR nodes.
143:     error_count: usize,

158: /// Incomplete Analysis Engine: a file-level rule that handles all 17
159: /// incomplete-analysis checks in a single pass.
160: ///
161: /// These checks represent linter-internal limits and cannot be disabled
162: /// by the user (`can_be_disabled() == false`).
163: pub struct IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
164:     config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig,
165: }

167: impl IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
168:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
169:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
170:         let rule_config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig = config.rule_params("INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS");
171:         Box::new(Self {
172:             config: rule_config,
173:         })
174:     }
175: 
176:     /// Walk the tree and collect all metrics in one pass.
177:     fn collect_metrics(&self, root: Node) -> TreeMetrics {
178:         let mut metrics = TreeMetrics::default();
179: 
180:         // Check last child of root for EOFMI.
181:         if let Some(last) = last_descendant(root) {
182:             metrics.last_node_is_error = last.is_error() || last.is_missing();
183:         }
184: 
185:         Self::walk_tree(root, &mut metrics, 0, 0, 0);
186:         metrics
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Recursive DFS traversal that collects node counts, error counts, and
190:     /// nesting depths in a single pass.
191:     fn walk_tree(
192:         node: Node,
193:         metrics: &mut TreeMetrics,
194:         paren_depth: usize,
195:         function_depth: usize,
196:         statement_depth: usize,
197:     ) {
198:         metrics.node_count += 1;
199: 
200:         if node.is_error() {
201:             metrics.error_count += 1;
202:         }
203: 
204:         // Track parentheses/bracket nesting depth (MDEEP).
205:         let new_paren_depth = match node.kind() {
206:             "parenthesis" | "arguments" | "matrix" | "cell" => {
207:                 let d = paren_depth + 1;
208:                 if d > metrics.max_paren_depth {
209:                     metrics.max_paren_depth = d;
210:                 }
211:                 d
212:             }
213:             _ => paren_depth,
214:         };
215: 
216:         // Track function nesting depth (DEEPN).
217:         let new_function_depth = if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
218:             let d = function_depth + 1;
219:             if d > metrics.max_function_depth {
220:                 metrics.max_function_depth = d;
221:             }
222:             d
223:         } else {
224:             function_depth
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Track statement nesting depth (DEEPS).
228:         let new_statement_depth = match node.kind() {
229:             "if_statement" | "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "switch_statement"
230:             | "try_statement" => {
231:                 let d = statement_depth + 1;
232:                 if d > metrics.max_statement_depth {
233:                     metrics.max_statement_depth = d;
234:                 }
235:                 d
236:             }
237:             _ => statement_depth,
238:         };
239: 
240:         // Recurse into children.
241:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
242:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
243:             Self::walk_tree(
244:                 child,
245:                 metrics,
246:                 new_paren_depth,
247:                 new_function_depth,
248:                 new_statement_depth,
249:             );
250:         }
251:     }
252: 
253:     /// Check maximum line length (TEXTL).
254:     fn check_line_lengths(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
255:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
256:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
257: 
258:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
259:             let char_len = line.chars().count();
260:             if char_len > self.config.max_line_length {
261:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
262:                     rule_id: "TEXTL",
263:                     message: format!(
264:                         "Line length ({char_len}) exceeds internal limit ({max})",
265:                         max = self.config.max_line_length
266:                     ),
267:                     severity: Severity::Error,
268:                     byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
269:                     line: line_idx + 1,
270:                     column: 1,
271:                     fix: None,
272:                 });
273:             }
274:             // +1 for newline character.
275:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
276:         }
277: 
278:         diagnostics
279:     }
280: 
281:     /// Scan source text for nested block comments (DEEPC).
282:     ///
283:     /// MATLAB block comments are `%{ ... %}`. Nesting is not allowed — a
284:     /// second `%{` inside an open block comment is an error.
285:     fn check_nested_block_comments(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
286:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
287:         let mut depth: usize = 0;
288:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
289: 
290:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
291:             let trimmed = line.trim();
292:             if trimmed == "%{" {
293:                 depth += 1;
294:                 if depth > 1 {
295:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
296:                         rule_id: "DEEPC",
297:                         message: format!(
298:                             "Block comments nested too deeply (depth {depth})"
299:                         ),
300:                         severity: Severity::Error,
301:                         byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
302:                         line: line_idx + 1,
303:                         column: 1,
304:                         fix: None,
305:                     });
306:                 }
307:             } else if trimmed == "%}" {
308:                 depth = depth.saturating_sub(1);
309:             }
310:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
311:         }
312: 
313:         diagnostics
314:     }
315: }

604: /// Find the last (rightmost, deepest) descendant node in a tree.
605: fn last_descendant(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
606:     let child_count = node.child_count();
607:     if child_count == 0 {
608:         return Some(node);
609:     }
610:     let last_child = node.child(child_count - 1)?;
611:     last_descendant(last_child)
612: }

1: //! # NOSEMI: Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: //!
3: //! In MATLAB, statements that produce output without a trailing semicolon will
4: //! print their result to the console. This is almost always unintentional in
5: //! production code and can cause significant performance degradation in loops.
6: //!
7: //! ## Examples
8: //!
9: //! Bad:
10: //! ```matlab
11: //! x = compute_value()
12: //! data = load('file.mat')
13: //! ```
14: //!
15: //! Good:
16: //! ```matlab
17: //! x = compute_value();
18: //! data = load('file.mat');
19: //! ```
20: //!
21: //! ## Configuration
22: //!
23: //! ```toml
24: //! [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
25: //! severity = "info"
26: //! ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
27: //! ```
28: 
29: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, Fix, NodeContext, Rule, Severity};
30: use serde::Deserialize;
31: 
32: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33: // Rule-specific configuration
34: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
35: 
36: /// Configuration for NOSEMI.
37: ///
38: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.NOSEMI]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
40: pub struct NosemiConfig {
41:     /// Function names to ignore (statements calling these functions won't be
42:     /// flagged even without a semicolon). Useful for intentional output
43:     /// functions like `disp`, `fprintf`, etc.
44:     #[serde(default)]
45:     pub ignore_functions: Vec<String>,
46: }
47: 
48: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49: // Rule implementation
50: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51: 
52: /// Rule NOSEMI: flags statements at the top level of a block that do not end
53: /// with a trailing semicolon.
54: ///
55: /// Targets `assignment`, `function_call`, and `command` nodes. Only fires when
56: /// the node is a direct child of `source_file` or `block` (i.e., at statement
57: /// level, not as a sub-expression).
58: pub struct Nosemi {
59:     config: NosemiConfig,
60: }
61: 
62: /// Statement-level node types that should typically end with a semicolon.
63: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["assignment", "function_call", "command"];
64: 
65: /// Parent node types that indicate statement-level context.
66: const STATEMENT_PARENTS: &[&str] = &["source_file", "block"];
67: 
68: impl Nosemi {
69:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
70:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
71:         let rule_config: NosemiConfig = config.rule_params("NOSEMI");
72:         Box::new(Self {
73:             config: rule_config,
74:         })
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: impl Rule for Nosemi {
79:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
80:         "NOSEMI"
81:     }
82: 
83:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
84:         "Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output"
85:     }
86: 
87:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
88:         Severity::Info
89:     }
90: 
91:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
92:         Category::Formatting
93:     }
94: 
95:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
96:         TARGET_NODES
97:     }
98: 
99:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
100:         let node = ctx.node;
101: 
102:         // Only fire at statement level: parent must be source_file or block.
103:         // This prevents flagging function_call nodes that are sub-expressions
104:         // (e.g., `x = foo(bar(1))` — bar(1) is not a statement).
105:         let is_statement_level = node
106:             .parent()
107:             .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
108:             .unwrap_or(false);
109: 
110:         if !is_statement_level {
111:             return Vec::new();
112:         }
113: 
114:         // If this is a function_call or command, check if the function name
115:         // is in the ignore list.
116:         if !self.config.ignore_functions.is_empty() {
117:             if let Some(func_name) = extract_function_name(node, ctx.source) {
118:                 if self.config.ignore_functions.iter().any(|f| f == func_name) {
119:                     return Vec::new();
120:                 }
121:             }
122:         }
123: 
124:         // Check if the statement is followed by a semicolon.
125:         let has_semicolon = has_trailing_semicolon(node, ctx.source);
126: 
127:         if has_semicolon {
128:             return Vec::new();
129:         }
130: 
131:         // Compute position for the diagnostic.
132:         let start = node.start_position();
133:         let end_byte = node.end_byte();
134: 
135:         vec![Diagnostic {
136:             rule_id: self.id(),
137:             message: self.description().to_string(),
138:             severity: self.severity(),
139:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..end_byte,
140:             line: start.row + 1, // tree-sitter is 0-indexed
141:             column: start.column + 1,
142:             fix: Some(Fix::insert(end_byte, ";")),
143:         }]
144:     }
145: }

151: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` or `command` node.
152: fn extract_function_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
153:     match node.kind() {
154:         "function_call" => {
155:             // The `name` field of a function_call node.
156:             let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
157:             // For simple calls, the name is an identifier.
158:             // For method calls (obj.method), take the full text.
159:             Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
160:         }
161:         "command" => {
162:             // The first child of a command is the command_name.
163:             let name_node = node.child(0)?;
164:             if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
165:                 Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
166:             } else {
167:                 None
168:             }
169:         }
170:         _ => None,
171:     }
172: }
173: 
174: /// Determine whether a statement node is followed by a semicolon.
175: ///
176: /// In tree-sitter-matlab's grammar, semicolons (`;`) and newlines are statement
177: /// terminators that appear as sibling nodes after the statement. We check the
178: /// source text immediately following the node for a `;` (skipping whitespace
179: /// on the same line).
180: fn has_trailing_semicolon(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
181:     // Strategy 1: Check next named/unnamed siblings for ";"
182:     let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
183:     while let Some(sib) = sibling {
184:         let kind = sib.kind();
185:         // Skip over comment nodes that might appear between statement and semicolon
186:         if kind == "comment" || kind == "line_continuation" {
187:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
188:             continue;
189:         }
190:         // If the next meaningful sibling is ";", the statement is terminated.
191:         if kind == ";" {
192:             return true;
193:         }
194:         // Any other sibling means no semicolon follows.
195:         break;
196:     }
197: 
198:     // Strategy 2: Fallback — scan the source text after the node end.
199:     // This handles cases where the semicolon might not be a separate node.
200:     let after = &source[node.end_byte()..];
201:     for ch in after.chars() {
202:         match ch {
203:             ';' => return true,
204:             // Stop at newline — semicolon must be on the same line.
205:             '\n' | '\r' => return false,
206:             // Skip inline whitespace.
207:             ' ' | '\t' => continue,
208:             // Any other character means something else follows.
209:             _ => return false,
210:         }
211:     }
212: 
213:     false
214: }

1: # NOSEMI - Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: 
3: **Default severity:** Info
4: **Auto-fix:** Yes
5: **Category:** Formatting
6: **Can be disabled:** Yes
7: 
8: ## What this rule does
9: 
10: Flags MATLAB statements that do not end with a trailing semicolon (`;`). This applies to statements that produce a value — primarily assignments, function calls, and commands at the statement level.
11: 
12: ## Why this matters
13: 
14: - **Performance**: In loops, unsuppressed output causes significant slowdowns due to console I/O on every iteration
15: - **Noise**: Unintended console output clutters the Command Window, making it harder to find real output
16: - **Intent**: Without a semicolon, it's ambiguous whether the output was intentional (for debugging) or accidental
17: - **CI/CD**: Stray output in automated MATLAB scripts can pollute logs or interfere with output parsing
18: 
19: ## Examples
20: 
21: ### Correct
22: 
23: ```matlab
24: x = compute_value();
25: data = load('file.mat');
26: result = process(data);
27: 
28: % Intentional output (configure ignore_functions)
29: disp('Processing complete');
30: fprintf('Result: %d\n', result);
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Incorrect
34: 
35: ```matlab
36: x = compute_value()
37: data = load('file.mat')
38: result = process(data)
39: ```
40: 
41: ### Fixed
42: 
43: ```matlab
44: x = compute_value();
45: data = load('file.mat');

5: # Rules Reference
6: 
7: ## Overview
8: 
9: mlt implements lint rules matching MATLAB's Code Analyzer checks for feature parity. Rules use the same check IDs as MATLAB (e.g., `NOSEMI`, `AGROW`, `naming.class.casing`) and are organized into categories.
10: 
11: ## Rule Table
12: 
13: | Rule ID | Category | Description | Default Severity | Auto-fix |
14: | ------- | -------- | ----------- | ---------------- | -------- |
15: | [NOSEMI](nosemi.md) | Formatting | Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output | Info | Yes |
16: 
17: ## Rule Categories
18: 
19: mlt organizes rules into the same categories as MATLAB's Code Analyzer:
20: 
21: | Category | Config Key | Description |
22: | -------- | ---------- | ----------- |
23: | Incomplete Analysis | `incomplete-analysis` | Internal linter limits and analysis failures |
24: | Syntax Errors | `syntax-errors` | Parser-level syntax validation |
25: | Language Specification | `language-specification` | Language constraint violations |
26: | Bugs | `bugs` | Likely bugs and logic errors |
27: | Custom Checks | `custom-checks` | Configurable code complexity/style metrics |
28: | Naming | `naming` | Naming convention enforcement |
29: | Compatibility | `compatibility` | Deprecated/removed functions and APIs |
30: | Forward Compatibility | `forward-compatibility` | Forward compatibility issues |
31: | Good Practices | `good-practices` | Common best practices |
32: | Unset Variables | `unset-variables` | Variables that may not be defined before use |
33: | Unused Constructions | `unused-constructions` | Dead code and unused constructions |
34: | Suggested Improvements | `suggested-improvements` | Suggestions for improved code patterns |
35: | Readability | `readability` | Readability improvements |
36: | Formatting | `formatting` | Code formatting suggestions |
37: | Performance | `performance` | Performance improvement suggestions |
38: | Code Generation | `code-generation` | MATLAB Coder constraints |
39: | Fixed-Point | `fixed-point` | Fixed-point toolbox specific |
40: | Deployment | `deployment` | MATLAB Compiler deployment constraints |
41: | System Objects | `system-objects` | System object validation |
42: | Unsupported | `unsupported` | Unsupported features |
43: | Behavior Changes | `behavior-changes` | Behavior changes between MATLAB versions |
44: | Configuration Issues | `configuration-issues` | Configuration file validation |
45: 
46: ## Severity Levels
47: 
48: Rules are categorized into three severity levels:
49: 
50: ### Error
51: 
52: Critical issues that likely indicate bugs or broken code:
53: 
54: - Code that will fail at runtime
55: - Language specification violations
56: - Syntax errors
57: 
58: ### Warning
59: 
60: Issues that affect code quality:
61: 
62: - Common bug patterns
63: - Good practice violations
64: - Deprecated function usage
65: 
66: ### Info
67: 
68: Low-priority suggestions:
69: 
70: - Formatting preferences
71: - Performance improvement hints
72: - Readability suggestions
73: 
74: ### Configuring Severity
75: 
76: Override default severities in `.mlt.toml`:
77: 
78: ```toml
79: [lint.rules]
80: NOSEMI = "error"    # Upgrade from info to error
81: ```
82: 
83: Or in a full table:
84: 
85: ```toml
86: [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
87: severity = "error"
88: ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf"]
89: ```
90: 
91: ### Category-Level Configuration
92: 
93: Enable, disable, or override severity for entire categories:
94: 
95: ```toml
96: [lint.categories]
97: performance = "off"           # Disable all performance rules
98: compatibility = "warn"        # Override all compatibility rules to warning
99: formatting = "info"           # Set all formatting rules to info
100: ```
101: 
102: Per-rule configuration always takes precedence over category-level settings.
103: 
104: See [Configuration](configuration.md) for full details.
105: 
106: ## Enabling and Disabling Rules
107: 
108: All rules are enabled by default. Disable individual rules:
109: 
110: ```toml
111: [lint.rules]
112: NOSEMI = "off"
113: ```
114: 
115: Or disable entire categories:
116: 
117: ```toml
118: [lint.categories]
119: behavior-changes = "off"
120: ```
121: 
122: ## Auto-fix Support
123: 
124: Rules marked with "Yes" in the Auto-fix column provide automatic fixes. Run mlt with `--fix` to apply them:
125: 
126: ```bash
127: mlt --fix src/**/*.m
128: ```
129: 
130: Fixes are applied atomically per file. Overlapping fixes are detected and the conflicting fix is skipped with a warning.
131: 
132: ## Adding New Rules
133: 
134: mlt uses auto-registration via the `inventory` crate. To add a new rule:
135: 
136: 1. Create a new module in `crates/mlt_rules/src/` (e.g., `agrow.rs`)
137: 2. Implement the `Rule` trait with a `from_config` factory
138: 3. Add `inventory::submit!(crate::RuleRegistration::new("AGROW", Agrow::from_config));` at the bottom
139: 4. Add documentation in `docs/agrow.md`
140: 
141: No manual edits to `lib.rs` are needed beyond adding the `pub mod` declaration.
142: 
143: See the [repository](https://github.com/watermarkhu/mlt) for the full development guide.

1: //! Configuration system for mlt.
2: //!
3: //! Supports `.mlt.toml` config files with the following schema:
4: //!
5: //! ```toml
6: //! [lint]
7: //! exclude = ["vendor/**", "test/fixtures/**"]
8: //!
9: //! [lint.rules]
10: //! M001 = "warn"           # shorthand: set severity
11: //! M002 = "off"            # disable a rule
12: //!
13: //! [lint.rules.M003]       # full table: severity + rule-specific params
14: //! severity = "error"
15: //! some_param = true
16: //! ```
17: //!
18: //! Rules access their typed parameters via [`Config::rule_params`], which
19: //! deserializes the rule's TOML table section into a `#[derive(Deserialize)]`
20: //! struct.

22: use std::collections::HashMap;

24: use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;

30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: // Config errors
32: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33: 
34: /// Errors that can occur during config parsing.
35: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
36: pub enum ConfigError {
37:     #[error("failed to parse config TOML: {0}")]
38:     Parse(#[from] toml::de::Error),
39: 
40:     #[error("invalid severity value '{0}' (expected: error, warn, info, off)")]
41:     InvalidSeverity(String),
42: }
43: 
44: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45: // Raw TOML file representation (what serde deserializes directly)
46: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
47: 
48: /// The raw `.mlt.toml` file structure.
49: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
50: pub struct ConfigFile {
51:     #[serde(default)]
52:     pub lint: LintSection,
53: }
54: 
55: /// The `[lint]` section of the config file.
56: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
57: pub struct LintSection {
58:     /// Glob patterns for files/directories to exclude from linting.
59:     #[serde(default)]
60:     pub exclude: Vec<String>,
61: 
62:     /// Per-rule configuration. Keys are rule IDs (e.g., "NOSEMI").
63:     /// Values are either a severity string or a full config table.
64:     #[serde(default)]
65:     pub rules: HashMap<String, RuleEntry>,
66: 
67:     /// Per-category configuration. Keys are category slugs (e.g., "performance").
68:     /// Values are severity strings ("off", "error", "warn", "info").
69:     #[serde(default)]
70:     pub categories: HashMap<String, String>,
71: }
72: 
73: /// A single rule's config entry — either a severity shorthand or a full table.
74: ///
75: /// Supports both:
76: /// - `M001 = "warn"` (shorthand)
77: /// - `[lint.rules.M001] severity = "error" ...` (full table)
78: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Clone)]
79: #[serde(untagged)]
80: pub enum RuleEntry {
81:     /// Shorthand: just a severity string ("error", "warn", "info", "off").
82:     Severity(String),
83:     /// Full config table with optional severity + rule-specific parameters.
84:     Full(toml::Table),
85: }

88: // Normalized config (what rules and the engine consume)
89: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
90: 
91: /// Resolved per-rule configuration.
92: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
93: pub struct RuleConfig {
94:     /// Whether the rule is enabled (false if set to "off").
95:     pub enabled: bool,
96:     /// Severity override (None = use rule's default).
97:     pub severity: Option<Severity>,
98:     /// Rule-specific parameters as a TOML table (deserialized by the rule).
99:     pub params: toml::Table,
100: }
101: 
102: impl Default for RuleConfig {
103:     fn default() -> Self {
104:         Self {
105:             enabled: true,
106:             severity: None,
107:             params: toml::Table::new(),
108:         }
109:     }
110: }
111: 
112: /// The resolved configuration passed to rule factories and the lint engine.
113: ///
114: /// Constructed from a [`ConfigFile`] (parsed `.mlt.toml`) via [`Config::from_toml`],
115: /// or created with [`Config::default()`] for unconfigured usage.
116: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
117: pub struct Config {
118:     /// Glob patterns for files/directories to exclude.
119:     pub exclude: Vec<String>,
120:     /// Per-rule configuration, keyed by rule ID.
121:     pub rules: HashMap<String, RuleConfig>,
122:     /// Per-category severity overrides, keyed by [`Category`].
123:     /// A value of `None` means the category is disabled ("off").
124:     pub categories: HashMap<Category, Option<Severity>>,
125: }

127: impl Config {
128:     /// Parse a `.mlt.toml` file's content into a resolved [`Config`].
129:     pub fn from_toml(content: &str) -> Result<Self, ConfigError> {
130:         let file: ConfigFile = toml::from_str(content)?;
131:         Self::from_config_file(file)
132:     }
133: 
134:     /// Convert a parsed [`ConfigFile`] into a resolved [`Config`].
135:     fn from_config_file(file: ConfigFile) -> Result<Self, ConfigError> {
136:         let mut rules = HashMap::new();
137: 
138:         for (rule_id, entry) in file.lint.rules {
139:             let rule_config = match entry {
140:                 RuleEntry::Severity(ref s) => {
141:                     let (enabled, severity) = parse_severity_string(s)?;
142:                     RuleConfig {
143:                         enabled,
144:                         severity,
145:                         params: toml::Table::new(),
146:                     }
147:                 }
148:                 RuleEntry::Full(table) => {
149:                     // Extract "severity" key if present, pass the rest as params.
150:                     let severity = if let Some(val) = table.get("severity") {
151:                         let s = val
152:                             .as_str()
153:                             .ok_or_else(|| ConfigError::InvalidSeverity(val.to_string()))?;
154:                         let (enabled, sev) = parse_severity_string(s)?;
155:                         if !enabled {
156:                             // Rule is disabled — record it and continue to the next rule.
157:                             rules.insert(
158:                                 rule_id,
159:                                 RuleConfig {
160:                                     enabled: false,
161:                                     severity: None,
162:                                     params: toml::Table::new(),
163:                                 },
164:                             );
165:                             continue;
166:                         }
167:                         sev
168:                     } else {
169:                         None
170:                     };
171: 
172:                     // All keys except "severity" are rule-specific params.
173:                     let params: toml::Table = table
174:                         .into_iter()
175:                         .filter(|(k, _)| k != "severity")
176:                         .collect();
177: 
178:                     RuleConfig {
179:                         enabled: true,
180:                         severity,
181:                         params,
182:                     }
183:                 }
184:             };
185: 
186:             rules.insert(rule_id, rule_config);
187:         }
188: 
189:         // Parse category overrides.
190:         let mut categories = HashMap::new();
191:         for (cat_name, severity_str) in file.lint.categories {
192:             let category: Category = cat_name.parse().map_err(|_| {
193:                 ConfigError::InvalidSeverity(format!("unknown category: {cat_name}"))
194:             })?;
195:             let (enabled, severity) = parse_severity_string(&severity_str)?;
196:             if enabled {
197:                 categories.insert(category, severity);
198:             } else {
199:                 // "off" means the category is disabled — store None.
200:                 categories.insert(category, None);
201:             }
202:         }
203: 
204:         Ok(Self {
205:             exclude: file.lint.exclude,
206:             rules,
207:             categories,
208:         })
209:     }

211:     /// Load and deserialize rule-specific parameters into a typed struct.
212:     ///
213:     /// If the rule has no config entry or the params table is empty, returns
214:     /// `T::default()`. If deserialization fails, logs a warning to stderr and
215:     /// returns `T::default()`.
216:     ///
217:     /// # Example
218:     ///
219:     /// ```ignore
220:     /// #[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
221:     /// struct M013Config {
222:     ///     max_line_length: Option<usize>,
223:     /// }
224:     ///
225:     /// let params: M013Config = config.rule_params("M013");
226:     /// ```
227:     pub fn rule_params<T: DeserializeOwned + Default>(&self, rule_id: &str) -> T {
228:         self.rules
229:             .get(rule_id)
230:             .and_then(|rc| {
231:                 if rc.params.is_empty() {
232:                     return None;
233:                 }
234:                 let value = toml::Value::Table(rc.params.clone());
235:                 match value.try_into::<T>() {
236:                     Ok(v) => Some(v),
237:                     Err(e) => {
238:                         eprintln!(
239:                             "mlt: warning: invalid config for rule {rule_id}: {e}; using defaults"
240:                         );
241:                         None
242:                     }
243:                 }
244:             })
245:             .unwrap_or_default()
246:     }

248:     /// Check whether a rule is enabled in this config.
249:     ///
250:     /// Returns `true` if the rule has no config entry (rules are enabled by default).
251:     pub fn is_rule_enabled(&self, rule_id: &str) -> bool {
252:         self.rules
253:             .get(rule_id)
254:             .map(|rc| rc.enabled)
255:             .unwrap_or(true)
256:     }

258:     /// Check whether a rule is enabled, considering both per-rule and per-category config.
259:     ///
260:     /// Resolution order:
261:     /// 1. Per-rule config takes precedence (if rule is explicitly configured).
262:     /// 2. Per-category config applies if the rule has no explicit config.
263:     /// 3. Default: enabled.
264:     pub fn is_rule_enabled_for_category(
265:         &self,
266:         rule_id: &str,
267:         category: Category,
268:     ) -> bool {
269:         // Per-rule override takes precedence.
270:         if let Some(rc) = self.rules.get(rule_id) {
271:             return rc.enabled;
272:         }
273:         // Check category-level config.
274:         if let Some(cat_severity) = self.categories.get(&category) {
275:             // None means category is disabled ("off").
276:             return cat_severity.is_some();
277:         }
278:         // Default: enabled.
279:         true
280:     }

282:     /// Get the configured severity override for a rule, if any.
283:     pub fn rule_severity(&self, rule_id: &str) -> Option<Severity> {
284:         self.rules.get(rule_id).and_then(|rc| rc.severity)
285:     }
286: 
287:     /// Get the effective severity for a rule, considering category overrides.
288:     ///
289:     /// Resolution order:
290:     /// 1. Per-rule severity override.
291:     /// 2. Per-category severity override.
292:     /// 3. None (use rule's default).
293:     pub fn effective_severity(&self, rule_id: &str, category: Category) -> Option<Severity> {
294:         // Per-rule override takes precedence.
295:         if let Some(rc) = self.rules.get(rule_id) {
296:             if rc.severity.is_some() {
297:                 return rc.severity;
298:             }
299:         }
300:         // Category-level override (flatten Option<Option<Severity>> → Option<Severity>).
301:         if let Some(cat_severity) = self.categories.get(&category) {
302:             return *cat_severity;
303:         }
304:         None
305:     }
306: }

312: /// Parse a severity string into (enabled, Option<Severity>).
313: ///
314: /// "off" → (false, None)
315: /// "error" → (true, Some(Error))
316: /// "warn" → (true, Some(Warning))
317: /// "info" → (true, Some(Info))
318: fn parse_severity_string(s: &str) -> Result<(bool, Option<Severity>), ConfigError> {
319:     match s.to_lowercase().as_str() {
320:         "off" | "false" | "disabled" => Ok((false, None)),
321:         "error" | "err" => Ok((true, Some(Severity::Error))),
322:         "warn" | "warning" => Ok((true, Some(Severity::Warning))),
323:         "info" | "note" => Ok((true, Some(Severity::Info))),
324:         other => Err(ConfigError::InvalidSeverity(other.to_string())),
325:     }
326: }
